precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with blasting and with mildew; the blasting and the mildew go into famine, exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops.
precepts.point: When Israel had sown, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up as grasshoppers for multitude, destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished. That goes right into the curses.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
What Midian did to Israel goes right into the curses. “The Lord shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.”

The blasting and the mildew go into famine, and that is exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops. When Israel had sown, they “came as grasshoppers for multitude”, “destroyed the increase of the earth”, and “left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.” “Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites”: the curse of Deuteronomy 28 carried out by an enemy's hand.

precepts.text: The Amorites go back into the Hamites: the lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan.
precepts.point: When Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent a prophet to remind them: I brought you up from Egypt out of the house of bondage, and I said, fear not the gods of the Amorites in whose land ye dwell, but ye have not obeyed my voice. The judgment came with a reason attached.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The prophet says, “fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell.” Who are the Amorites? They go back into the Hamites. “And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite.”

The lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan. These are the people whose land the Most High gave Israel when he “drave them out from before you”, and whose gods Israel was told not to fear. Instead, Israel did not obey his voice, and the judgment came with that reason attached.

precepts.text: The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven; they go and come as they please, change forms, vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night.
precepts.point: The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
An angel of the Lord “sat under an oak which was in Ophrah” and then “appeared unto” Gideon. What is an angel? “Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.”

The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven. They go and come as they please, change forms, and vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night. That is the kind of being that sat down under the oak while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, hiding his own harvest from the Midianites, and greeted him, “The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.”

precepts.text: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares, just as Tobias in the book of Tobit entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself.
precepts.point: The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon did not know at first who was sitting under that oak. “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.”

It is the same with Tobias in the book of Tobit, who entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself. An angel of the Lord came and sat in Ophrah, appeared to a man threshing wheat by the winepress, and spoke with him as a stranger might. That is why we are told to “Let brotherly love continue” and not to forget to entertain strangers.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards and not sons. That is why the other nations never suffer the judgments we suffer: the chastening of the Most High does not pertain to them, but he chastens us because we are his sons.
precepts.point: Gideon answers, oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon asks, “if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us?” A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us? Here is the answer. “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.”

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

That is why the other nations never suffer the judgments we suffer. The chastening of the Most High does not pertain to them; he chastens us because we are his sons. All this befell Israel in Gideon's day, and befalls us now, not because the Lord has forsaken us, but because he receives us as sons.

precepts.text: No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous but grievous, and it does look grievous to all of us; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness, which is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised thereby.
precepts.point: Gideon answers, oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” Our fathers “for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.”

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous.” It does look grievous to all of us, just as it looked to Gideon with Midian eating up the land. But “nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” That peaceable fruit is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised by the chastening. So “why then is all this befallen us” has an answer: for our profit.

precepts.text: Have I been a wilderness unto Israel, a land of darkness? The Lord asks, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee.
precepts.point: Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon says “the Lord hath forsaken us”, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. Hear how the Lord answers it: “O generation, see ye the word of the Lord. Have I been a wilderness unto Israel? a land of darkness? wherefore say my people, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee?”

He is asking, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, “We are lords; we will come no more unto thee.” God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

precepts.text: My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns that can hold no water. The water is the word, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves, Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in.
precepts.point: Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The Lord names the two evils: “For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.”

The water is the word. We forsook the fountain of living waters, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves: Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in. None of them can hold water.

So when Gideon says “the Lord hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites”, he has it backwards, as our people do today. It is not that the Lord forsook us; “they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters.”

precepts.text: Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called; God hath chosen the foolish, the weak, the base, and the despised things of the world to confound the mighty.
precepts.point: The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon answers the Lord with his pedigree: “my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.” That is a defeated mentality, and it is the very thing Paul answers. “For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.”

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are.”

The poor family in Manasseh and the least in his father's house is exactly whom God chooses. We all have to overcome that defeated mentality, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

precepts.text: Hath not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him? The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?”

Gideon's family was “poor in Manasseh”, and the Lord still said, “Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?” The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him. Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High. The poor of this world are the ones he has chosen to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.text: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God; you could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord.
precepts.point: Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.”

What man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. You could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord. So Gideon being the least in his father's house, with no prestige to his name, was no hindrance to his calling, and it is no hindrance to yours. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

precepts.why:
“And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

The servant formed from the womb to bring Jacob again to the Lord is glorious in the eyes of the Lord. Gathering Israel back is the highest honor on earth. Gideon was sent to save Israel from the hand of the Midianites and thought himself too poor and too small for it; but to be sent by the Lord for Israel is glory in his eyes, whatever man thinks of your family.

precepts.text: Samuel looked on Eliab and thought, surely the Lord's anointed is before him, but the Lord said, look not on his countenance or the height of his stature; man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. You short brothers can be great leaders.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
When Samuel came to anoint a king, “he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the Lord’s anointed is before him. But the Lord said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.”

The Lord did not look on Gideon's poor family or his place as the least in his father's house. He looked upon him and saw a mighty man of valour, and said, “Go in this thy might.” Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. You short brothers can be great leaders.

precepts.text: There are celestial bodies and bodies terrestrial; our earthly bodies are made of the ground, but the angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing.
precepts.point: Gideon brings a kid and unleavened cakes, and the angel touches the flesh and the cakes with the end of his staff; fire rises up out of the rock and consumes them, and the angel departs out of his sight, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The angel touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes with the end of his staff, “and there rose up fire out of the rock”, and then he “departed out of his sight”, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

“There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.” Our earthly bodies are made of the ground, terrestrial. The angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, bring fire out of a rock, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing.

Christ said of the little ones, “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.”

Every one of us that has repented has a guardian angel assigned to minister to us and nudge us in the way the Lord wants our life to go. The angel of the Lord ministered to Gideon at the rock in Ophrah; their angels behold the face of the Father in heaven and minister to his little ones now.

Notice this: even before the split of the kingdom, the tribes that would become the northern kingdom were already dabbling with Baal. Gideon's own father had an “altar of Baal” and a grove by it, worshipping the Lord in some fashion while holding onto the idol, and the men of the city worshipped it too, which is why Gideon had to throw it down by night.

That is why it was such an easy transition when Jeroboam “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” The north had been dealing with Baal long before the split ever happened; Jeroboam only gave them what they were already used to.

precepts.text: The same power made Aaron's rod bud, bloom blossoms, and yield almonds overnight.
precepts.point: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The Lord commanded the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleased: on the fleece only with the earth dry beside it, and then dry on the fleece with dew on all the ground. God can do whatever he wants; infinite power.

The same power made Aaron's rod bud overnight: “on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.” A dead rod bore fruit in a night, just as a bowl full of water was wrung out of a fleece on dry ground.

The dew landing where he pleases, a rod budding overnight, the shadow going backward on the sundial: it is all the same infinite power. God did so that night for Gideon because he can do whatever he wants.

points: The men demand his death, but Joash stands up for his son: will ye plead for Baal? If he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar. Obviously he is no god; he is an idol. So that day Gideon was named Jerubbaal, saying, let Baal plead against him.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: The Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east gathered and pitched in the valley of Jezreel, but the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon; he blew a trumpet, and Abiezer, Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali came up to meet him.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Those tribes are warriors; do not get it twisted. You see how Zebulun and Naphtali, who are in the south Americas right now, get down: that warrior spirit is still in them, only right now it has turned on each other, and the Most High is going to correct it and turn it right again.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.
